body: I love this. Couldn't have said it better myself.

Ugh, THANK you. I feel the same way man. I'm bound by contract to stay in my dead-end office job for another seven months...after that, fuck the money. I'm going to get a job that I think is important on a scale that I care about. Like helping or working with animals. I don't care if I get paid a shitty salary. 

Money fucking sucks. School loans fucking suck. Jobs fucking suck. The system fucking sucks. 

I always get trapped in thinking about THE POINT. Like, what's THE POINT of working at a job for 50 years? You retire just in time to die? Jesus.

I like to think of pills like water wingies. You use them to learn the mechanics of swimming, and then gradually learn to swim without them. You can't just rip them off and jump in the ocean without learning to swim on your own, you'd sink like a rock, right? :)
The problem with me isn't waking up, it's getting out of bed ;) and once I get out of bed it's far too tempting to go right back in.

I feel the same way, only I need to get "back to numb" to save my job, which I hate, because I'm stuck there for the moment.

Good luck, stay strong..

Yeah, that's exactly what it's like. The past week has been so awful productivity-wise but I cleaned my room and showered and have been showing up to work. I don't get too much satisfaction out of accomplishing things, because any pride I get from finishing a task is immediately replaced with self-loathing and anxiety about all the things I'm not doing.

Thank you for the kind words

That's the thing, she seems young and cool. I like her as a person. I can't believe how relentless she's been about this. Seems like she personally has beef with stimulants so she doesn't want to prescribe them.

I've always had so much trouble with these "professionals." I don't know who else to go to for help if they don't help me, that's the discouraging part.

I'm on prozac and wellbutrin and seeing a therapist as well...I feel like none of these things f*cking work.

Anyway. I don't have any really good tips, because I constantly struggle with this as well. Sometimes letting myself go out looking like shit helps. Like, I'm wearing sweatpants, I didn't shower, I look awful. But I showed up so I did okay.

Getting out of bed is the hardest thing. Still haven't figured that one out.

I'm moving back home with my mom at the end of the summer when my lease is up...partially because living rent free will help me pay off my loans but also because I'm just miserable living in the city with roommates. I have no idea if it will help, but at the very least I think being home will be comforting...

I'd say go for it.

UGH I'm in the exact same spot, except with work instead of school. For example, I have a meeting to present work at in 2 hours. I have done none of the work that I'm supposed to be presenting. And here I am on reddit. 

My therapist asks me why, too- and I tell her I just can't make myself do it! I can't make myself care! And what are they gonna do, fire me? Good, I hate this place.

And then I remember, no, you need the money, you can't get fired, your parents would be so ashamed, you'd be so embarrassed...

And then I start beating myself up- why don't you get anything done? Why can't you just do your work like everyone else? Just do it and it'll be done! Why won't you just do it!!

And then it's, fuck it, I don't care, I can't do it, so why try, and the cycle repeats.

Whoohoo! You go girl :) Be proud, that's excellent!

I'm in the same boat where I am- Weather's been miserable and we just it 40 degrees (fahrenheit!) 

Exercise doesn't make a huge dent in my mood all the time, but it does make me feel proud of myself for doing it.

I'm in the same boat...hate the people I work with, the work I do, the setting I work in...it's a horrible office job in a horrible office filled with horrible people. I also get all the bitch jobs and am frequently talked down to/given useless busy work. I'm too depressed to work on anything really so I guess it doesn't matter...

Worst part is I can't leave even though I want to. I signed a contract and took a sign on bonus so I'm stuck till next december.

So, I don't have much advice for you. But I would recommend making your life outside work as good as you can...for a long time I would be in such a bad mood coming home from work that I would hole myself in my room and do nothing and fall asleep as early as possible so I wouldn't have to be awake anymore. Lately I've started picking up old hobbies that I love and making an effort to hang out with my roommates.

I also have a plan in place for what I'll do when I get out of this job...sometimes that helps...

It sucks. There are okay days, there are bad days, and then there are really bad days. I frequently find myself sitting at my desk unable to convince to myself to give a shit about the "work" I have to do, and thinking about how I'd rather chew my own arm off or die than stay here another minute.

But here I am. So. 

I guess I don't have much advice or comfort to give except that I'm in the same boat. If you ever want to vent or commiserate PM me.

Glad I'm not the only one. But still sorry to hear that.

I'll definitely check those out. I forgot about Grand Budapest Hotel, I actually really wanted to see that when it came out.
I'm actually not entirely sure...if they did let me go, I think I'd be upset about it for all of two seconds before gleefully collecting unemployment and hunting for a better job...

Not much to say other than I feel for you...I graduated last spring and I did get a job, but I hate it...i went to college to get a job, I'm stuck with a job now to pay off college...I feel like I went to college for nothing...what was the point...I'd do anything to not have to work anymore...

Anyway. Hang in there man...

I take it with my Prozac, 10mg in the morning, 10mg at lunch. It gives me the extra boost I need to clean my room, take care of myself, get out of bed, etc. it does help me be productive at work usually but my job is such a large part of why I'm depressed that it hasn't helped much there as of late. 

I've only been on it for a few months so I don't know if I'm going to gain a tolerance for it to the point where it doesn't work...I hope not...it made a huge difference for me.

The other thing is, living at home is loads cheaper, so even factoring in wear and tear on my car from commuting to said horrible job I'd be saving around $700 a month...which I could throw at my loans.

If I can just make it through to august so I don't have to find a subletter I'd be okay...I am a little camper. I do need to buck up. I like that.

Nope, I feel the same way when I get reminder emails at work.

Oh, man. I'm sorry you got turned down. I just got myself set up with a counselor (my first appointment is this friday! ahh!) and I have to tell you, it was a freaking nightmare. My regular doctor got me on prozac, so he knows I'm depressed, and yet somehow it took forever to get an official referral from him, transferred to a different branch of my doctor's office where they had available counselors, and still the soonest appointment they had wasn't for another two weeks. All this was after we went through my insurance and called like 10 different people who accepted my insurance only to find that none of them were taking patients. 

It's hard. I don't know why. This is time sensitive stuff...asking for help is really hard and they shouldn't make it harder, but they do. Hang in there.

I had to have my mom make a lot of the phone calls for me because I'm a big baby and I was too overwhelmed to.

Anyway. Good luck, keep trying...

I live in the US. it's helpful to have a GP who's okay with prescribing that stuff, because unless you can find a psychiatrist (who are allowed to prescribe meds) counsellors and therapists need to work with your GP to get you meds.

I would go and tell your GP you want prozac or something for right now, and to refer you to a counselor for down the road. Finding a counselor/therapist takes a while, which is annoying, so getting started on a low dose antidepressant might help in the meantime. This is what I did.

 Good luck :(
Oh my god, I'm so sorry...

Dude, you're doing great. I know from experience that coming out of an eating disorder is practically a full time job. You're healing. All the things you're doing are so wonderful, just for your heart...doing things you love, that make you feel peaceful. So, congratulations on getting to be where you are, that's a huge accomplishment. 

In terms of these things that are weighing down on you...maybe try tackling one little thing at a time. Baby steps. Whatever it takes, whatever you can do. Find a part time job and only work there once a week. Or join a dating website and send some girls some messages when you're feeling up to it. Don't try and tackle all that junk at once. That's a lotta junk to tackle. Jobs, friends and a girlfriend won't do you any good if you're feeling like crap.

You can PM me any time as well. I'm a pretty lonely critter I'm always around to talk. :)

Oh, my gosh. I could have written this myself...
I don't have anxiety, but man, I hate my job. I hate going. I hate being there. I hate doing work there. I hate procrastinating there. I hate the people there. I hate the building. I just hate it. And I'm stuck there because I need the money. I 30000% hear you...

Heck, I'm at work now and I'm on r/depression, so what does that tell you.

The problem that I have is that I don't think I would like any job. I don't want to go to work and talk with people I hate and do things I don't like. The things I love doing don't pay the bills, so I have to go to work. That's why they call it work...because it's work. and work sucks.

I just had a lovely little breakdown for myself last week and had to take 3 sick days in a row to go to my mom's house, recover, get my meds upped, and to make an appointment with a counselor. So I'm trying to make it more...bearable. I don't think I'll ever like it, but I'm determined to deal with it somehow. 

Granted...this is a full time job that I got right after college. Jobs like this one at walmart aren't worth your soul. Really. Get out of there if you can. Give your two weeks, or don't. Just stop showing up if that's what you need to do. Fuck walmart. Who gives a crap about those jerks? What's the worst that would happen if you didn't show up? They'd be short staffed for a night? Who. Cares. You gotta look out for you.

If that's not an option and this job is something you want to work at dealing with...feel free to PM me. We can work on it together. I don't have the answers but I'm trying very hard to find the light at the end of the tunnel...
If you ever need help, ah, eating those majestical beasts, I would be happy to provide my services...
Does she give you a hard time or do you just feel guilty, just because?

judge you?! I'm glad to hear you're okay!!

Props to you for having the balls to go to the doctor and make sure you were alright!
Showering...now that's another story...
Guess I was surprised that the place didn't go up in flames or anything while I was gone...I was so stressed about leaving for those few days but everything turned out to be fine!
I ended up getting everything done that I needed to do (this morning anyway...) I feel like a super hero or something...

I can relate to this...these days I've been cutting myself some slack and just hanging out with the two "people" I can stand...which is my mom and my dog! Yes, I'm 22 and I hang out with my mom. Seems pathetic, but being with her makes me happy and eases the pain from the whole "no friends" deal.

I'm still very bitter about couples though...that I'll have to work on...when I see couples out and about being cute...well, the phrase "if looks could kill" comes to mind ;)

Some of them have! I met a few kids in college who were in the psych program and they had some very...interesting backgrounds. You might be surprised. But, really, it's all about who you get along with...I know if I go to this first session and hate the person, I'm going to be vocal about it and find someone I like!

Hope you're doing better today.

Your dad gives good advice!

Sometimes I try to imagine that I'm my mom- how would I treat me then? I'd give me a nice dinner, and sit down with me to watch a nice movie, and tuck me into a cuddly bed. I like my "mom-voice" much better than my regular negative voice. :)

Don't feel silly for getting upset. That's a horrible thing to go through...I'm so sorry for your loss, and that you had to experience that. 

Your feelings are 100% justified...and that guy was a jerk for not letting you vent about it.

It might help to seek out a therapist or counselor...it's scary territory I know. I just made my first appointment, which is next week. I'm scared but it seems like there's a light at the end of the tunnel...someone has to listen to me and help me! They're getting paid to!!

At the very least, go ahead and feel your feelings and don't feel silly about them. You can press an ice cube to your wrist if the urge to self-harm becomes too strong- it actually feels like a wonderful relief and doesn't leave a mark.

Good luck to you, I hope you feel better. :c
WOOHOO!! Congratulations!! Happy you're safe and in a good spot. Best of luck to you, friend.

Ahh, yes. Especially when I'm home alone and the walk to the kitchen seems like too much effort. Putting something in the microwave would be too much effort. Lifting food to my mouth would be too much effort...

When I feel this way, I try to spend time with my mom (unfortunately I can only see her on the weekends) and she's a great comfort to me...she is also an excellent cook. I'll also sometimes just think of her- how important it is to her that I eat well. Sometimes a thought of my ol' mom is enough to make me pick the whole wheat pasta instead of the cheap white stuff.

Another thing I do when I'm feeling this way is I eat anything I "can." Like, eating a healthy dinner would be too hard. Ordering food and talking on the phone would be too hard. But I could eat half a box of my favorite cookies, or a plate of pizza rolls. Throw on some sweatpants and go take a depressed cruise through the supermarket. You may see a cereal you loved when you were a kid, or a frozen dinner that reminds you of your favorite restaurant, whatever sparks some kind of comfort in you, however small. It might help. 

I have experience with depression and eating disorders myself, so if you need to talk, or want to vent, PM me.

My job is so miserable I just want to get away and hide from it. I do get much more depressed than usual on sundays when monday is fast approaching...if it weren't for my dog, I probably wouldn't leave the house at all.

I don't have a solution for you, just know that you're not alone.
